title: AI 要跨越盧比孔河了嗎？自我成長的 AI 離我們多遠 (下集)

topic_alignment.paraphrase: After describing fixed and external editors, Lee turns back to systems in which the updater can change. This cue bridges the fixed-editor discussion and the two examples. The current harness serving as its own editor was first explained at 2043.741 seconds.

Having named two papers at 2110.007 seconds, Lee explains that once the harness becomes h′ the rule used for the next edit is h′. The new version reads its own code at 2124.622 seconds to produce a successor.
Lee introduces the example from Hyperagents. At 2168.900 seconds he refers to the candidate pool. At 2184.815 seconds he says that the agent changes the sampling algorithm itself.

Lee turns to experimental results. He identifies random sampling for green at 2207.004 seconds, the agent-modified strategy for orange beginning at 2208.706 seconds, and the manually designed blue strategy at 2237.034 seconds. The paper supplies test scores and uncertainty.

Lee turns from editing a harness to updating parameters, naming Learning to Self-Evolve at 2259.423 seconds. At 2293.624 seconds the revised harness is evaluated. The performance difference becomes the editor’s reward at 2300.331–2302.166 seconds.

topic_alignment.paraphrase: At 176, 180, 182, 185, 187, 190, 196, 200 and 204 seconds the talk shows the three-column design comparison. The legend uses green for learnable parts and gray for fixed parts. The rightmost column includes the optimization module itself among the editable components.
The frame at 362 seconds shows the results table with DROP F1 and accuracy columns for MGSM, MMLU and GPQA. Check the paper’s Table 1 for the reported numerical values.
